subject: Workplace Skills
title: CC and BCC Etiquette
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: CC and BCC Etiquette.

hook.text: A junior analyst hit Reply All to 400 people. The thread spiraled for three days.

buildup.text: CC means 'for your awareness.' BCC means 'hidden copy.' Misuse creates chaos or distrust.

discovery.text: Only CC people who need to stay informed. If they don't need to act, they probably don't need the email.

twist.text: BCC is useful for large distribution lists but feels sneaky in small conversations. Use it carefully.

climax.text: Before adding someone to CC, ask: will they thank me or resent me for this notification?

punchline.text: Every CC is a tiny demand on someone's time.

quiz.question: When should you CC someone on an email?
options: Always, to keep everyone in the loop
Only when they need to stay informed about the topic
